q.t: A can do a job in 5 days. What fraction of the job does A do in one day?
q.e: The job is shared equally over 5 days, so each day gets one fifth.

q.t: A and B can each do a job alone in 10 days. How long do they take together (in days)?
q.e: Each does 1/10 a day, together 2/10 = 1/5 a day: 5 days.

q.t: A can do a job in 6 days. What fraction is done in 2 days?
q.e: 1/6 each day, so 2/6 = 1/3 in two days.

q.t: A pipe fills a tank in 4 hours. What fraction of the tank does it fill in 1 hour?
q.e: Equal amounts each hour: one quarter.

q.t: A can do a job in 12 days and B in 6 days. How long do they take together (in days)?
q.e: 1/12 + 1/6 = 3/12 = 1/4 of the job a day: 4 days.

q.t: A does 1/8 of a job each day. How many days does the whole job take?
q.e: Eight eighths make the whole job.

q.t: A and B together do 1/4 of a job each day. How many days do they take to finish it?
q.e: Four quarters make the whole job.

q.t: A takes 20 days for a job. How many days does half the job take?
q.e: Working at a steady rate, half the job takes half the time.

q.t: A tap fills 1/3 of a tank every hour. How long does it take to fill the tank (in hours)?
q.e: Three thirds make a full tank.

q.t: A works twice as fast as B. B takes 12 days for a job. How long does A take (in days)?
q.e: Twice the speed means half the time.

q.t: A can do a job in 15 days and B in 30 days. How long do they take together (in days)?
A and B together take 8 days; A alone takes 12 days. How long does B alone take (in days)?
A, B and C can do a job alone in 6, 12 and 4 days. How long do all three take together (in days)?
Two pipes fill a tank in 20 minutes and 30 minutes. How long do they take together (in minutes)?
A pipe fills a tank in 10 hours and a leak can empty it in 15 hours. With both working, how long does the tank take to fill (in hours)?
q.e: Net each hour: 3/30 − 2/30 = 1/30. So 30 hours — the leak works against the pipe.

q.t: A can do a job in 18 days. He works for 6 days. What fraction of the job is left?
A and B together take 6 days; B alone takes 10 days. How long does A alone take (in days)?
A does 1/3 of a job in 5 days. How long does the whole job take him (in days)?
q.e: Three thirds, at 5 days each.

q.t: Two taps fill a cistern in 15 hours and 10 hours. How long do they take together (in hours)?
A can do a job in 24 days and B in 16 days. How long do they take together (in days)?
A can do a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. They work together for 4 days, then A leaves. How many more days does B need?
q.e: Together 1/6 a day → 4/6 = 2/3 done. B does the last 1/3 at 1/15 a day: 5 days.

q.t: A and B take 12 days, B and C take 15 days, and C and A take 20 days. How long do all three take together (in days)?
q.e: Adding the three pairs counts everyone twice: 5/60 + 4/60 + 3/60 = 1/5. So all three do 1/10 a day.

q.t: A and B take 12 days, B and C take 15 days, and C and A take 20 days. How long would A take alone (in days)?
q.e: All three do 1/10 a day; B and C do 1/15. A alone: 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30.

q.t: A can do a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. They do it together and earn ₹3000. Find A’s share (in ₹).
q.e: Pay is shared by work done. Rates 1/10 : 1/15 = 3 : 2, so A gets 3/5 of 3000.

q.t: Pipes A and B fill a cistern in 12 and 15 hours; pipe C empties it in 20 hours. With all three open, how long does it take to fill (in hours)?
A is 50% more efficient than B. B takes 30 days for a job. How long does A take (in days)?
q.e: A works 1.5 times as fast, so takes 30 ÷ 1.5 = 20 days.

q.t: A can do a job in 20 days. He works for 5 days and B finishes the rest in 12 days. How long would B take for the whole job (in days)?
q.e: A does 1/4, leaving 3/4. B does 3/4 in 12 days, so the whole job takes 16.

q.t: A pipe fills a tank in 8 hours, but because of a leak it takes 10 hours. How long would the leak take to empty the full tank (in hours)?
q.e: Leak’s rate = 1/8 − 1/10 = 1/40 of the tank an hour.

q.t: A and B together take 10 days; A alone takes 15 days. They earn ₹4500 for the job. Find B’s share (in ₹).
q.e: B’s rate = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30. A : B = 1/15 : 1/30 = 2 : 1, so B gets one third.

q.t: 3 men OR 5 women can do a job in 12 days. How long do 6 men and 5 women take together (in days)?
q.e: 6 men = 2 teams of ‘3 men’; 5 women = 1 more such team. Three teams take 12 ÷ 3 = 4 days.

q.t: A, B and C together take 6 days. A alone takes 18 days and B alone takes 27 days. How long does C alone take (in days)?
A and B together can do a job in 30 days. They work for 20 days, then B leaves and A finishes the rest in 20 more days. How long would A take alone (in days)?
q.e: In 20 days they do 2/3. A does the last 1/3 in 20 days, so the whole job takes him 60.

q.t: Pipe A fills a tank in 30 minutes and pipe B in 45 minutes. Both are opened together. After how many minutes should B be closed so that the tank is full in exactly 20 minutes?
q.e: A runs all 20 minutes and fills 20/30 = 2/3. B must fill 1/3, which takes 45 ÷ 3 = 15 minutes.

q.t: 12 men can finish a job in 18 days. After 6 days, 4 more men join. How many more days does the job take?
q.e: Work left = 12 × 12 = 144 man-days. With 16 men: 9 days.

q.t: A works twice as fast as B and three times as fast as C. All three together take 6 days. How long does A take alone (in days)?
q.e: If A does 1 unit a day, B does 1/2 and C 1/3: together 11/6 units a day. Job = 6 × 11/6 = 11 units — 11 days for A.

q.t: A can do a job in 16 days and B in 12 days. With C’s help they finish in 4 days. How long would C take alone (in days)?
A (16 days), B (12 days) and C together finish a job in 4 days and are paid ₹4800. Find C’s share (in ₹).
q.e: In 4 days A does 4/16 = 1/4 and B does 4/12 = 1/3. C does the rest: 5/12 of the job, so 5/12 of ₹4800.

q.t: A is three times as fast as B, and so finishes a job 60 days sooner than B would. How long do they take working together (in days)?
q.e: B takes 3 times as long: 3a − a = 60, so A takes 30 days and B 90. Together: 1/30 + 1/90 = 4/90, i.e. 22.5 days.

q.t: A cistern normally fills in 9 hours, but a leak in the bottom makes it take 10 hours. How long would the leak take to empty the full cistern (in hours)?
q.e: Leak’s rate = 1/9 − 1/10 = 1/90 of the cistern an hour.

q.t: Two taps run at 6 litres and 4 litres a minute into a 300-litre tank, while a drain lets out 5 litres a minute. How long does the empty tank take to fill (in minutes)?
q.e: Net flow in = 6 + 4 − 5 = 5 litres a minute. 300 ÷ 5 = 60 minutes.
